info.title: LabLink API
info.description: Order lab tests through LabLink. Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <API key>`. Sandbox and production are separate base URLs with separate keys. Docs: https://lablink.caregap.io/docs · for agents: https://lablink.caregap.io/llms.txt

servers.description: Sandbox — Synthetic data only. Nothing reaches a real lab or a real patient, and nothing is billed. Use a sandbox key.
Production — Real patients and real orders. Available once your account is live. Use a production key.

post.description: Creates a patient you can order tests for. Send your own id for the patient as `externalId`: it is unique in your organization, so retrying a create with it returns `conflict` and the existing id instead of a duplicate, and you can find the patient by it later. Without an `externalId`, every call creates a new patient, even one with the same name and date of birth — LabLink never merges or blocks on similarity. Only `firstName`, `lastName` and `dateOfBirth` are required; unknown fields are rejected so a typo cannot be silently dropped.

dateOfBirth.description: Date of birth, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Not in the future.

sexAtBirth.description: Sex assigned at birth. Defaults to `Unknown`.

enum: Native Hawaiian or other Pacific Islander

ssnLast4.description: Last 4 digits of the SSN, exactly 4 digits. Write-only: responses show `ssnLast4Masked`.

externalId.description: Your own id for this patient, e.g. the id in your system. Up to 64 letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `:` or `-`. Unique in your organization: a second create with the same value returns `conflict`. Find the patient by it with `GET /patients?externalId=`.

400.description: `invalid_request`: A required field is missing, a value is not one of the allowed values, `dateOfBirth` is not `YYYY-MM-DD` or is in the future, or a field name is unknown. `param` names the field.

401.description: `unauthorized`: The key is missing, revoked, expired, or belongs to the other environment.

409.description: `conflict`: A patient with this `externalId` already exists. `existingId` is its id — fetch it rather than creating again.

502.description: `platform_unavailable`: The lab network did not answer in time.

post.description: Orders lab tests for a patient — in one call. Name the tests by Quest code (`{ "code": "6399" }`) or test id, as `GET /tests` returns them; a code must match exactly. If any test asks questions (see `GET /tests/{id}`), send every answer in `answers`: the order is not created until all are answered. Send `providerNpi` for the ordering provider; with only one provider in your organization it is chosen for you. Send the patient’s diagnoses as `diagnosisCodes`, ICD-10-CM codes such as `E11.9` (up to 10): they go to the lab with the provider’s authorization, and payors need them to show the testing is medically necessary. Send the patient’s address as `patientAddress` the first time you order for them: it is saved to their record. Patients in RI are not served. Every sandbox organization has a test provider, Test Physician, NPI `1336176510`: send it as `providerNpi`, or leave `providerNpi` out while it is your only provider. LabLink then completes the questionnaire and the provider authorization itself. If it cannot — an NPI that cannot order, a question it could not match — the order is still created and `actionRequired` says what is left and which call finishes it. Sandbox only for now: on production this returns `not_available` until production billing is in place.

patientId.description: The `id` of the patient the tests are for, from `POST /patients`.

tests.description: The tests to order, 1–25. Each is `{ "code": "6399" }` (a Quest order code) or `{ "id": "92314142" }` (a test id) — both as `GET /tests` returns them.

providerNpi.description: The NPI of the ordering provider. Needed when your organization has more than one; with exactly one, it is chosen for you. In sandbox, use the test provider's: `1336176510`.

diagnosisCodes.description: The patient’s diagnoses, as ICD-10-CM codes, up to 10: `["E11.9", "Z00.00"]`, with or without the dot. Sent to the lab with the provider’s authorization; payors, insurance above all, need them to show medical necessity. Each is checked before the order is created. Find codes with `GET /diagnosis-codes`.

billing.description: Who pays for the testing: `client` (client bill: Quest invoices your organization); `patient` (patient cash: The patient pays Quest at their visit); `insurance` (patient insurance: Quest bills the patient’s insurance; the patient pays the rest). Defaults to `client`. See Billing in the docs.

insuranceIds.description: With `billing: "insurance"`: which of the patient’s coverages to bill, primary first. Left out, LabLink bills their active coverage in precedence order.

patientAddress.description: Where the patient is: `{ "line1": "…", "city": "…", "state": "TX", "postalCode": "78701" }`. Saved to the patient’s record, never kept by LabLink. Required unless the patient already has an address on file. Patients in `RI` are not served.

answers.description: Answers to the tests’ ask-at-order-entry questions, from `GET /tests/{id}`: `[{ "questionId": "92321198", "value": "180" }]`. Required when any ordered test has questions — the order is not created until every one is answered.

400.description: `invalid_request`: A field is missing or malformed, a code matches no orderable test, a question has no answer (the message lists them), an answer is for a question none of the tests asks, `providerNpi` is not a valid NPI, or a `diagnosisCodes` entry is not an ICD-10-CM code the lab knows, or is a category rather than a code that can be ordered (the message names its place in the list). Nothing is created.

401.description: `unauthorized`: The key is missing, revoked, expired, or belongs to the other environment.

403.description: `not_available`: Called on production. Orders are sandbox-only until production ordering opens.

502.description: `platform_unavailable`: The lab network did not answer in time.

get.description: Returns your organization’s orders, most recently changed first. Each carries its `status` and `currentStep`; `steps` is empty in a list — fetch the order for them. Keep requesting the next `page` while `hasMore` is true.

401.description: `unauthorized`: The key is missing, revoked, expired, or belongs to the other environment.

get.description: Returns an order’s status and every step it goes through. `status` is where the order is, in LabLink’s vocabulary: `created`, then `awaiting_collection` once Quest has the requisition and the patient can be drawn, then `results_final`; or `cancelled`. `currentStep` is the step it is waiting on and `steps` lists them all. Poll this to follow an order until its results are in.

get.description: Returns the requisition for the order as a PDF. The requisition Quest’s order produced, as a PDF: what the patient brings to the draw. It exists once the order reaches `awaiting_collection`, which the `order.awaiting_collection` webhook announces; fetch it then. Before that the answer is `not_ready`. It contains the patient’s details: store and send it as you would any patient record.

post.description: Finishes the questionnaire when `actionRequired.type` is `answer_questions`. Answer the questions listed in `actionRequired.questions`, by their `id`. Send `providerNpi` and `diagnosisCodes` too, so the provider step — which a create that stopped at the questions never reached — finishes in the same call, with them. LabLink then carries on with the remaining steps and returns the order. Sandbox only for now.

providerNpi.description: The ordering provider’s NPI, to finish the provider step too. In sandbox: `1336176510`.

diagnosisCodes.description: The order’s ICD-10-CM codes, sent with the provider step. Send them again: the create stopped before the provider step, so the ones sent with it were not used.

400.description: `invalid_request`: `answers` is missing, empty or malformed, or a `diagnosisCodes` entry is not an ICD-10-CM code the lab knows, or is a category.

post.description: Finishes the provider authorization when `actionRequired.type` is `choose_provider`. Send the NPI of one of the providers listed in `actionRequired.providers` — in sandbox, the test provider, Test Physician, NPI `1336176510` — and the order’s `diagnosisCodes`. LabLink authorizes the order under them, with those diagnoses, and carries on with the remaining steps. With only one provider in your organization `providerNpi` can be left out. Sandbox only for now.

providerNpi.description: The ordering provider’s NPI. Needed when your organization has more than one. In sandbox: `1336176510`.

diagnosisCodes.description: The order’s ICD-10-CM codes, e.g. `["E11.9"]`, from `GET /diagnosis-codes`. Send them again here: an order stopped before its provider step has none yet.

get.description: Finds ICD-10-CM codes to send with an order. Search by a code or part of one, with or without the dot (`E11`, `E11.6`, `E116`), or by words from its description (`diabetes`). A code search matches every code containing it, so `A01.2` also finds `C7A.012`: the code itself comes first, then codes that start with it. A category such as `E11` cannot be ordered, only the codes under it: it is left out when they are on the page, and refused on an order. Send the ones that apply as `diagnosisCodes` on `POST /orders`. LabLink checks every code before the order is created: one the lab does not know is refused with `invalid_request`, naming its place in the list, and nothing is created. Works on sandbox and production; no order is needed.

parameters.description: A code or part of one, e.g. `E11` or `E11.65`, or words from its description, e.g. `type 2 diabetes` (letters, digits, spaces and hyphens).

code.description: The ICD-10-CM code, with its dot, e.g. `A01.2`. Send it in `diagnosisCodes`.

description.description: What the code means, e.g. `Paratyphoid fever B`.

400.description: `invalid_request`: `search` is missing, shorter than two characters, or holds characters other than letters, digits, spaces and hyphens; or `page`/`limit` is out of range.

post.description: Finishes the Choose payment step when `actionRequired.type` is `choose_billing`. `POST /orders` sets billing itself (`billing`, default `client`), so you need this only when an order stopped at payment. LabLink submits the choice and carries on with the remaining steps. Sandbox only for now.

billing.description: `client`: Quest invoices your organization. `patient`: the patient pays Quest at their Patient Service Center visit. `insurance`: Quest bills the patient’s insurance on file and collects any balance at the visit. See Billing in the docs.

insuranceIds.description: With `insurance`: which coverages to bill, primary first, from `GET /patients/{id}/insurance`. Left out, every active one is billed in precedence order.

400.description: `invalid_request`: `billing` is missing or not `client`, `patient` or `insurance`; or the patient has no active insurance to bill, or an `insuranceIds` entry is not one of theirs.

apiKey.description: An API key from the LabLink console’s API keys page, for the same environment as the base URL.

id.description: The patient id. Use it to fetch the patient and, later, to order for them.

externalId.description: Your id for the patient, if you gave one.

ssnLast4Masked.description: Masked, e.g. `***-**-1234`. The full SSN is never returned.

id.description: The test id, e.g. `92314142`. Use it with `GET /tests/{id}` to read the test’s questions, or to order it as `tests: [{ "id": "…" }]`.

name.description: The test’s name, as Quest lists it, e.g. `CBC (H/H, RBC, INDICES, WBC, PLT)`.

status.description: Where the order is, in LabLink’s vocabulary: `created` (being set up, until Quest has the requisition), `awaiting_collection` (Quest has it; the patient can be drawn), `results_final` (results are in) or `cancelled`. `collected`, `received_by_lab`, `results_partial` and `corrected` are reserved for when the lab network reports them. Branch on this, and on `actionRequired`, rather than on step names.

currentStep.description: The step it is waiting on, e.g. `Provider authorization`.

steps.description: Every step of the order, in order, each with its `status`. Empty in lists.

actionRequired.description: Set when the order is waiting on you: `{ type: "answer_questions", questions }` or `{ type: "choose_provider", providers }`, with a `message` saying which call finishes it. Null otherwise.

type.description: A stable name for the step: `patient`, `questionnaire`, `provider_authorization`, `requisition`, `results`, … Null for one LabLink does not know.

name.description: What the step is, as the lab network names it, e.g. `Requisition Creation`.

id.description: The question id. Answer with it in `POST /orders`.

text.description: The question as Quest asks it.

allowableAnswers.description: What an answer may be, as Quest defines it. `{ "text": {} }` means free text.

order.description: Where it comes among the test’s questions.

value.description: Free text, or an object in the form the question’s `allowableAnswers` describes.

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. `TX`. `RI` is not served.

TestRef.description: A test to order: by Quest order code, or by test id — exactly one.

message.description: What to change. Written to be acted on.

param.description: The field at fault, when there is one.

requestId.description: Also in the `LabLink-Request-Id` header. Quote it to support.
